question: A 24-year-old woman at 9 weeks presents with incomplete abortion. The cervical os is open and she is haemodynamically stable. Which uterine evacuation technique is currently the PREFERRED method for this gestational age?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Sharp curettage is associated with higher rates of uterine perforation and Asherman syndrome compared to suction methods. It is no longer the preferred first-line approach for early pregnancy.

Correct. MVA using a 60 mL syringe and flexible Karman cannula is the WHO-recommended preferred method for first-trimester evacuation. It is safer, can be done under local anaesthesia with paracervical block, and has lower complication rates than sharp curettage.

answers.text: Medical management with misoprostol only, without any surgical backup

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Medical management is an option for selected cases, but an open os with active haemorrhage in an incomplete abortion is better served by immediate evacuation. Medical management without surgical backup is not appropriate for this clinical scenario.

Hysterotomy is a major surgical procedure reserved for very specific situations such as cervical stenosis preventing any vaginal approach — it is not a first-line option for a routine incomplete abortion at 9 weeks.

overallFeedback.feedback: MVA (manual vacuum aspiration) has largely replaced sharp curettage for first-trimester evacuation in evidence-based practice. Remember: same effectiveness, less trauma, less anaesthesia requirement.
Correct. MVA is the WHO-recommended gold standard for first-trimester evacuation — safe, effective, requires only local anaesthesia, and minimises Asherman risk.
